This guide, prepared as educational guidance from TrustUSAHub, explains practical ways to approach Cash App account security and responsible payment management. It focuses on knowledge that can be applied in daily life rather than promotional activities. The goal is to make digital money management easier to understand. By learning the principles behind secure account use, users can become more deliberate when sending payments, receiving money, managing personal information, and responding to unexpected account messages.

  1. Understanding Cash App Account Safety in Everyday Life Cash App account safety begins with understanding what information and activities are connected to an account. A typical account may involve a phone number or email address, authentication information, payment activity, contacts, and potentially linked financial accounts or cards. Each element deserves appropriate attention. A useful first step is recognizing that an account should be treated as personal financial access. The account should be accessed through legitimate Cash App channels, and login or verification information should not be casually shared with other people. Why Account Awareness Matters Digital financial literacy means understanding how a financial application works before relying on it for everyday transactions. Users should know how to: ● Sign in through the official application or legitimate website. ● Review account and privacy settings. ● Confirm payment information before completing transactions. ● Keep authentication information private. ● Recognize unexpected account communications. ● Review transaction history regularly. ● Know how to contact official support when assistance is necessary. These habits are useful beyond Cash App. The same principles can be applied to banking applications, online shopping accounts, email services, and other platforms containing private information. Learning the Difference Between Convenience and Responsibility Mobile payment applications are convenient because they allow transactions to happen quickly. However, speed should not replace careful checking. Before completing a payment, users can pause for a moment and verify the recipient, amount, and purpose. This simple habit creates a more thoughtful approach to digital money. For example, someone splitting a restaurant bill with friends might check the recipient's information and the exact amount before selecting the payment option. A few seconds of attention can make the transaction easier to understand and document later. Building Digital Financial Literacy Using Cash App can also become an opportunity to learn basic financial organization. Transaction histories can help users understand where money is going, how frequently payments occur, and which expenses are shared with other people. For younger adults learning to manage personal finances, these habits can support broader skills such as budgeting, record keeping, and responsible digital communication.

  2. Creating Strong Account Protection Habits Strong account protection is based on several simple behaviors rather than one single setting. A good approach combines private authentication information, device security, software updates, and careful communication. Users should create account credentials that are difficult for other people to guess. Passwords should not be reused across important services, particularly when those services contain personal or financial information. Protecting Login Information Authentication information should remain private. Avoid sharing passwords, verification codes, PINs, or other account-access information through text messages, social media conversations, email, or phone calls. A legitimate support process should not require a user to casually disclose private authentication details to an unknown person. Good account habits include: ● Use unique credentials where available. ● Keep PINs private. ● Never publish authentication codes online. ● Avoid storing sensitive information where other people can easily see it. ● Sign out of accounts on devices that are shared. ● Review connected devices and settings when the application provides those options. Securing the Mobile Device Cash App security is also connected to the security of the phone itself. A device should have a screen lock, such as a PIN, password, fingerprint, or another supported authentication method. Automatic locking can add another layer of privacy when the phone is left unattended. Users should also keep their mobile operating system and applications updated. Updates may include improvements to security, stability, and privacy. Installing applications from legitimate sources is another useful habit. Avoid downloading unfamiliar applications simply because someone sends a link recommending them. Using Authentication Features Carefully Cash App may provide security and authentication options that can change over time. Users should review the current settings available within the official application. When an authentication feature is enabled, the user should understand what information is required to access the account and what happens if the device or phone number changes. Keeping recovery information current can make account management easier when legitimate access problems occur. Developing a Personal Security Routine Instead of checking security settings only after a problem appears, users can create a simple routine. For example, once every few months, review: ● Account information. ● Authentication settings. ● Device access. ● Linked payment methods. ● Notification preferences. ● Recent transactions. ● Privacy settings. This turns account protection into a normal digital housekeeping activity.

  3. Making Payments Carefully and Accurately One of the most important practical skills when using Cash App is confirming transaction details before sending money. A payment may be completed quickly, so users should avoid treating the send button as something to select automatically. Reviewing the information first is a useful everyday practice. Confirm the Recipient Before sending a payment, check the recipient's identifying information displayed by the application. When paying someone for the first time, take additional care to ensure the account belongs to the intended person. If the payment is related to a purchase, service, event, or shared expense, confirm the payment details through an independent communication channel when appropriate. For example, if a friend provides a payment username through a group conversation, compare it with information you already know about that person rather than assuming every similar username belongs to them. Confirm the Amount Numbers deserve careful attention. A payment of $25 and a payment of $250 can look similar when someone is moving quickly. Before confirming a transaction, check the amount and consider whether it matches the original agreement. This is particularly useful when paying rent contributions, event expenses, freelance invoices, group purchases, or shared household costs. Review the Payment Purpose Adding an appropriate note can help users remember why a payment was made. A short description such as “July utilities,” “dinner split,” or “design project” can make transaction records easier to understand later. Users should avoid putting unnecessary sensitive information into payment notes. A transaction description should communicate the purpose without exposing private details. Keep Records Organized Cash App transaction history can provide a useful record of digital payments. Users should periodically review their activity and compare it with their personal budgeting system. For people managing freelance work or shared expenses, keeping appropriate records can simplify financial organization. The purpose is not merely to monitor spending. Reviewing transactions can help people recognize patterns and develop stronger money-management habits.

  4. Protecting Personal Information and Privacy Privacy is an important part of responsible Cash App usage. Digital payment services can involve information about transactions, contacts, devices, and account activity. Users should understand what information they provide and avoid sharing more information than necessary. Share Only Necessary Information When someone needs to send money to you, provide only the information necessary for the intended transaction. There is generally no reason to publish passwords, PINs, verification codes, or complete financial credentials in a public location. Likewise, avoid posting screenshots that reveal private account details. Before sharing a screenshot, examine it carefully for: ● Full names. ● Phone numbers. ● Email addresses. ● Payment identifiers. ● Transaction information. ● Account balances. ● QR codes. ● Other personal details. Be Thoughtful on Social Media Social media posts can reveal more information than intended. A person might share a screenshot of a successful payment without realizing that it contains identifying information. A good digital privacy habit is to inspect images and messages before publishing them. The same principle applies to community groups, messaging applications, online marketplaces, and professional networks. Understand Privacy Settings Cash App settings can change as the service evolves. Users should review the current privacy and communication options available in their own account rather than relying on outdated instructions. Pay attention to options involving notifications, contacts, discoverability, and communication. Understanding settings is an important digital-life skill because privacy controls are common across modern platforms. Limit Unnecessary Communication Unexpected messages involving money should be treated thoughtfully. A message claiming that an account needs immediate action should not automatically be accepted as genuine. Instead:

  5. Stop and read the message carefully.

  6. Avoid clicking unfamiliar links.

  7. Open the official Cash App application directly if account information needs to be checked.

  8. Review the account independently.

  9. Use official support channels when assistance is required. This approach reduces the chance of making a decision based solely on pressure or urgency.

  10. Recognizing Unusual Messages and Financial Communication Learning to identify questionable communication is one of the most valuable digital skills associated with Cash App account safety. Fraudulent messages can imitate companies, friends, family members, employers, or service providers. They may use familiar logos, convincing language, or urgent requests. Common Warning Signs Users should pay attention when a message: ● Requests a verification code. ● Asks for a password or PIN. ● Claims immediate action is required. ● Requests money unexpectedly. ● Provides an unfamiliar login link. ● Uses unusual grammar or formatting. ● Promises money in exchange for a payment. ● Asks the recipient to move a conversation to an unrelated platform. ● Creates pressure to act before checking the information. One warning sign does not automatically prove that communication is fraudulent. The important lesson is to verify information independently. Use Independent Verification Suppose a person receives a message that appears to come from a friend requesting money. Instead of responding immediately, they can contact the friend through a known phone number or another established communication method. Similarly, if a message claims to come from Cash App, the user can open the official application directly rather than following a link supplied in the message. Independent verification is a valuable skill in many areas of life, including email, social media, online shopping, and workplace communication. Avoid Pressure-Based Decisions Financial decisions deserve attention. Messages that create urgency can make people act before thinking. A useful personal rule is: Pause → Verify → Decide. The pause creates time for careful thinking. Verification confirms whether the information is genuine. The final decision can then be based on evidence rather than pressure. Teach the Habit to Family Members Digital financial education is particularly valuable in families. Parents, guardians, older relatives, and educators can discuss examples of suspicious messages without asking anyone to disclose private account information. Simple conversations can help people understand why authentication codes should remain private and why unexpected payment requests deserve verification.

  11. Developing Everyday Financial Skills Through Responsible Cash App Use Cash App can be viewed not only as a payment application but also as an environment where people practice modern financial habits. Responsible use can support skills involving budgeting, record keeping, communication, and planning. Budgeting and Spending Awareness Transaction records can help users understand recurring expenses. For example, someone might notice that they frequently send small payments for transportation, meals, entertainment, or shared purchases. Seeing these transactions together can make spending patterns easier to understand. Users can organize expenses into categories such as: ● Food. ● Transportation. ● Household expenses. ● Entertainment. ● Education. ● Freelance work. ● Gifts. ● Shared expenses. This can support a broader monthly budget. Learning to Communicate About Money Many payment situations involve another person. Friends may split bills. Roommates may divide household. expenses. Freelancers may receive payments for completed work. Family members may share costs. Clear communication can prevent confusion. Before sending or requesting money, agree on: ● The amount. ● The purpose. ● The expected date. ● Who is responsible for the payment. ● Any relevant documentation. These are useful interpersonal skills regardless of which payment service is being used. Building Record-Keeping Skills Keeping financial records is valuable for students, employees, independent workers, and households. A simple spreadsheet or budgeting application can complement transaction histories. For example, a person might record: Date Purpose Amount Category July 5 Shared dinner $32 Food July 8 Household contribution $75 Household July 12 Transportation $20 Travel July 18 Freelance payment $180 Income The exact system is less important than consistency. Learning From Small Transactions Small digital payments can accumulate over time. Reviewing them periodically can help users understand how everyday decisions affect monthly finances. This encourages a useful financial principle: small transactions deserve attention too.

Case Studies and Practical Examples Case Study 1: Splitting a Restaurant Bill Alex goes to dinner with three friends. After the meal, everyone agrees to divide the cost. Instead of sending money immediately, Alex confirms the amount with the group. Alex then checks the friend's payment information before completing the transaction. After sending the payment, Alex reviews the transaction and keeps the record available for personal budgeting. The lesson is simple: convenience works best when paired with verification. Case Study 2: Receiving a Suspicious Account Message Jordan receives a message claiming to be from Cash App. The message says that Jordan must provide a verification code immediately. Jordan does not share the code. Instead, Jordan opens Cash App directly and checks the account. Jordan then uses an official support method if additional assistance is necessary. The educational lesson is that authentication information should remain private, even when a message appears official. Case Study 3: Managing Shared Household Expenses Sam and a roommate regularly divide household expenses. At the end of each month, Sam reviews digital payments and categorizes them as utilities, groceries, transportation, or other household expenses. This process makes it easier for both people to understand what has already been paid. The broader lesson is that digital payment records can support better financial organization when used consistently. Case Study 4: A Freelance Worker Taylor performs occasional freelance design work and receives digital payments. Taylor records the date, amount, client-related description, and category for each payment. Taylor avoids placing confidential project information into payment notes. At the end of the month, these records are compared with Taylor's broader financial records. The educational benefit is improved organization. Digital payments become part of a structured record-keeping system rather than isolated transactions. Case Study 5: Helping a Family Member Learn A family member who is new to digital payments receives a suspicious message. Instead of simply telling them what to do, another family member explains three principles:

  1. Never share authentication codes.
  2. Check unexpected requests independently.
  3. Open official applications directly instead of relying on unfamiliar links. The learner can then apply those principles to other financial and online services. This demonstrates why digital literacy is more valuable than memorizing one specific procedure.

Step-by-Step Guide to Using Cash App More Safely The following process provides a practical routine for everyday account management. Step 1: Secure Your Device Use a strong device lock and keep the phone's operating system current. Do not leave an unlocked phone unattended when financial applications are accessible. Step 2: Review Cash App Security Settings Open the official Cash App application and review the current security and authentication options. Choose appropriate settings based on the features available to your account. Step 3: Keep Authentication Information Private Never voluntarily provide passwords, PINs, or verification codes to another person. If someone asks for an authentication code, stop and independently verify why it is supposedly required. Step 4: Confirm Payment Details Before sending money, review: ● Recipient. ● Amount. ● Payment purpose. ● Any relevant note. ● Available balance or funding source. Take a few seconds to make sure everything matches your intention. Step 5: Review Incoming Requests Do not automatically approve or respond to an unexpected payment request. Consider who sent it, why they sent it, and whether the request matches something you were expecting. When necessary, verify the request using a known communication channel. Step 6: Inspect Account Activity Review recent transactions periodically. Look for activity you do not recognize and investigate it through official account-support processes when necessary. Step 7: Protect Screenshots and Shared Information Before sharing a screenshot, remove or conceal unnecessary personal information. Never share an image containing authentication codes or other credentials. Step 8: Keep Software Updated Install legitimate updates for both your mobile operating system and Cash App. Updates help maintain current functionality and may include important security improvements. Step 9: Learn the Official Support Process If an account question occurs, use Cash App's current official support resources. Avoid relying on strangers in social media comments who claim they can fix account problems. Step 10: Make Verification a Habit The most useful long-term practice is simple: Check before you send. This habit can become automatic over time and can also be applied to banking, shopping, email, and other online services.

Frequently Asked Questions

  1. What is the best way to use a Cash App account safely in 2026? Start with basic account protection. Keep authentication information private, secure your mobile device, use official applications, review payment information before confirming transactions, and monitor account activity regularly. The exact Cash App settings and features can change, so users should rely on the current options presented within the official service.
  2. Should I share my Cash App PIN or verification code? No. Authentication information should remain private. A PIN or verification code is intended to help establish that the legitimate account holder is accessing the account. If someone unexpectedly asks for such information, stop and independently verify the request rather than providing the code.
  3. How can I verify a Cash App payment request? First, consider whether you were expecting the request. Check the sender information and the stated purpose.
  4. How can Cash App transaction history help with financial education? Transaction history can help users understand everyday spending and payment patterns. Reviewing transactions can support budgeting, expense categorization, household record keeping, and financial planning. It can also help people become more aware of how small purchases contribute to monthly spending.
  5. What should I do if I receive a suspicious Cash App message? Do not immediately click unfamiliar links or provide private account information. Open the official application directly and check the account independently. If assistance is necessary, use the official support options provided by Cash App.
  6. Can these safety habits be used with other online accounts? Yes. Many of the principles are broadly useful. Keeping authentication information private, using strong device protection, verifying unexpected requests, checking transactions, maintaining updated software, and limiting unnecessary personal information are valuable habits for many digital services.

Conclusion and Final Thoughts Learning how to use Cash App accounts safely in 2026 is ultimately about developing practical digital and financial habits. The most valuable lessons are straightforward: protect authentication information, secure the device used to access the account, verify recipients and payment amounts, review account activity, protect personal information, and independently check unexpected requests. These practices can improve more than the way someone uses a payment application. They can strengthen broader digital literacy. item.title: 프로그래머스 편지
item.content:encoded:
문제

내가 생각했을때 문제에서 원하는부분

머쓱이는 할머니께 생신 축하 편지를 쓰려고 합니다.
        할머니가 보시기 편하도록 글자 한 자 한 자를 가로 2cm 크기로 적으려고 하며, 편지를 가로로만 적을 때, 축하 문구 message를 적기 위해 필요한 편지지의 최소 가로길이를 return 하도록 solution 함수를 완성해주세요.

내가 이 문제를 보고 생각해본 부분

main 메서드 안에서는 Main133 클래스의 객체 T를 생성한다.
        그 후 객체 T를 통해 solution 메서드를 호출하면서 테스트 케이스 문자열인 "happy birthday!"와 "I love you~"를 전달한다.
        System.out.println을 사용해 solution 메서드가 계산하여 반환한 결과값을 콘솔 창에 출력한다.
        solution 메서드는 매개변수로 문자열 message를 전달받는다.
        자바의 length() 메서드를 이용해 전달받은 문자열의 전체 글자 수를 구한다.
        이때 공백도 하나의 문자로 정확하게 포함된다.
        구한 글자 수에 한 글자당 필요한 가로 크기인 2를 곱해준다.
        계산된 최종 결과값을 answer 변수에 저장한 뒤 반환한다.

코드로 구현

class Solution {
        public int solution(String message) {
        int answer = message.length() * 2;
        return answer;
        }
        }

프로그래머스 코드

package programmers.programmers2;
        
        // 프로그래머스 편지
        public class Main133 {
        public static void main(String[] args) {
        Main133 T = new Main133();
        System.out.println(T.solution("happy birthday!")); // 30
        System.out.println(T.solution("I love you~")); // 22
        }
        
        public int solution(String message) {
        int answer = message.length() * 2;
        return answer;
        }
        }

위에 있는 코드를 변경한 코드

마무리

코드와 설명이 부족할수 있습니다. 코드를 보시고 문제가 있거나 코드 개선이 필요한 부분이 있다면 댓글로 말해주시면 감사한 마음으로 참고해 코드를 수정 하겠습니다.

  • ★ 장기보유특별공제시에도 이월과세면 증여한 배우자 또는 직계존비속이 취득한 날부터, 가업상속공제는 상속해준 피상속인이ㅏ 취득한 날부터 기산한다.

3) 1세대 1주택 특례

  • n: 장기보유특별공제 1세대 1주택의 경우는 보유기간 3년이상에 보유기간 중 거주기간이 2년이상이어야한다.

4) 적용 배제 — 기본공제와 갈리는 지점

  • ★★ 장기보유특별공제를 적용하지 않는 대상은 미등기, 국외, 조정대상지역 1세대 2주택, 1세대 3주택이상이고 양도소득공제는 미등기만 적용배제한다. 양도소득공제에 국외나 조정지역도 기본공제가 가능하다는 사실을 잊으면 안된다.

5) 공제율 계산

  • ⚠️ 장기보유특별공제를 계산할때 공제율은 거주연수 * 2%(1세대 1주택 보유3, 거주2 이상은 4) + 보유연수 * 2%(1세대 1주택 보유3, 거주2 이상은 4)로 합쳐서 구해야한다. 그리고 이를 차액에 곱한다.

1-2. 양도차익 계산의 특례

💡 전체를 다 과세하지 않고 "과세할 부분만 잘라내는" 안분 계산 구간.

1) 고가주택

  • ★ 비과세요건을 충족한 고가주택의 양도차익은 양도차익에서 12억 초과비율만큼 안분한다. 이때 고가주택판단기준이 양도소득세의 경우는 실지거래가액이고 부동산임대업은 기준시가이다.

2) 부담부증여

  • ★ 부담부증여에서는 양도가액은 평가한 가액 * 채무액/증여가액이고 취득가액은 취득가액 * 채무액/증여가액이다.
    • 예) 5억 아파트를 전세보증금 3억과 함께 넘기면 → 3/5는 양도(양도세), 2/5는 증여(증여세)

1-3. 부당행위계산의 부인

💡 "가족끼리 값을 조작하거나, 한 다리 건너 팔아서 세금을 줄인 것"을 세법이 되돌려 놓는 장치.

1) 특수관계인 간 고가양수·저가양도

  • ★★ 특수관계인간 고가양수, 저가양도의 부당행위계산 부인의 경우 시가와 거래가액의 차액이 3억 이상이거나 시가의 5%에 상당하는 금액 이상인 경우는 시가로 계산하고 거래가액이 아님에 유의해야한다.

2) 이월과세 vs 증여 후 우회양도의 부인

  • ⚠️ 이월과세는 수증자의 배우자거나 이혼한 배우자인 경우에 적용하고 양도일까지의 기간이 10년이내이면 증여세를 필요경비에 산입해준다. 따라서 수증자 한명이 다 내므로 연대납세의무도 없고 취득시기를 증여자가 취득한 시기로 볼 뿐이다. 반면 특수관계인간 양도행위부인은 증여자의 취득시기를 취득시기로 보는 것은 동일한데 그냥 수증자가 없는셈 친다. 즉 증여를 하지 않은 것으로 보아 증여세를 다시 돌려주고 납세도 증여자가 한다. 이때 수증자는 완전히 빠지고 연대납세의무만 질 뿐이다.
구분 이월과세 증여 후 우회양도의 부인
증여의 존재 인정 (수증자가 판 것) 부정 (증여자가 직접 판 것)
증여세 필요경비에 산입 돌려줌(환급)
납세의무자 수증자 증여자
연대납세의무 없음 수증자가 짐
취득시기 증여자가 취득한 때 증여자가 취득한 때

구분 실익: 증여세를 "빼주느냐(경비) vs 돌려주느냐(환급)"가 두 제도를 가르는 단일 기준.

3) 우회양도 부인의 적용 배제

  • 양도행위부인 사례에서 양도소득이 해당 수증자에게 실질적으로 귀속된 경우는 증여자의 이득을 위한게 아니므로 양도행위의 부인 적용을 배제한다.

1-4. 양도차손의 공제

💡 손해 본 것을 어디서, 어떤 순서로 빼주느냐의 문제.

1) 공제 대상

  • ★ 양도차손은 각호의 소득별로 양도차손을 "양도소득금액"에서 공제할 수 있다. 양도차익에서 공제하는게 아니다.

2) 공제 순서

  • ★ 양도차손의 공제순서는 발생한 자산과 같은 양도세 세율을 적용받는 양도소득금액에서 우선 공제한다.
    • 예) 같은 세율끼리 먼저 상계 → 그래도 남으면 다른 세율 자산으로 넘어감

1-5. 양도로 보지 않는 경우

  • ★★ 경공매 후 본인이 재취득하면 이는 양도로 보지 않는다.
    • 예) 내 건물이 경매에 넘어갔는데 내가 다시 낙찰받으면, 소유자가 바뀐 적이 없으니 양도가 아님

⚠️ 확인 필요

원문은 그대로 두었고, 아래만 별도로 확인 바랍니다.

① 장기보유특별공제 공제율 계산식 (1-1 / 5))

원문: "거주연수 × 2% + 보유연수 × 2% (1세대 1주택은 각 4%)"

  • 일반 자산(표1): 보유연수 × 2%만 적용. 거주기간은 계산에 들어가지 않는다. 3년 이상부터, 최대 30%.
  • 1세대 1주택(보유 3년 + 거주 2년 충족, 표2): 보유연수 × 4% + 거주연수 × 4%, 각 최대 40% → 합 최대 80%.

즉 "거주연수 × 2%"라는 항은 존재하지 않습니다. 거주기간이 공제율에 들어오는 건 1세대 1주택 표2에서만입니다. (공제율 수치는 현행 기준 확인 필요)

② 이월과세 적용 대상 (1-3 / 2))

원문: "수증자의 배우자거나 이혼한 배우자인 경우에 적용"

  • 이월과세 대상은 배우자 또는 직계존비속입니다. 직계존비속이 빠져 있습니다.
  • 배우자는 증여 당시 혼인관계가 소멸된 경우(이혼)를 포함하되, 사망으로 소멸된 경우는 제외합니다.
  • 참고로 1-1 / 2)에는 "배우자 또는 직계존비속"으로 정확히 적혀 있습니다. 같은 논점을 두 번 적으면서 한쪽이 줄어든 케이스입니다.

③ "이를 차액에 곱한다" (1-1 / 5))

공제율을 곱하는 대상은 양도차익입니다. (고가주택이면 12억 초과분으로 안분한 양도차익)

④ 조정대상지역 다주택 중과 관련 (1-1 / 4))

조정대상지역 1세대 2주택·3주택 이상에 대한 장기보유특별공제 배제는 중과세 적용을 전제로 합니다. 중과 적용 시행 상태는 개정·유예가 반복된 영역이라 현행 기준 확인 필요합니다. 조문 자체를 묻는 문제는 원문대로가 맞습니다.

public class Solution
        {
        public int solution(int a, int b, int c, int d)
        {
        int answer = 0;
        List<int> arr = new List<int>() { a, b, c, d };
        arr.Sort();
        if (arr[0] == arr[3])
        {
        answer = 1111 * arr[0];
        }
        else if (arr[2] == arr[3] && arr[0] != arr[3] && arr[1] == arr[2])
        {
        answer = (10 * arr[3] + arr[0]) * (10 * arr[3] + arr[0]);
        }
        else if (arr[0] == arr[1] && arr[0] != arr[3] && arr[1] == arr[2])
        {
        answer = (10 * arr[0] + arr[3]) * (10 * arr[0] + arr[3]);
        }
        else if (arr[0] == arr[1] && arr[2] == arr[3])
        {
        answer = (arr[0] + arr[2]) * Math.Abs(arr[0] - arr[2]);
        
        }
        else if (arr[0] != arr[1] && arr[1] != arr[2] && arr[2] != arr[3] && arr[0] != arr[3])
        {
        answer = arr.Min();
        }
        else if (arr[0] == arr[1] && arr[1] != arr[2] && arr[2] != arr[3] && arr[0] != arr[3] && arr[1] != arr[3])
        {
        answer = arr[2] * arr[3];
        }
        else if (arr[1] == arr[2] && arr[0] != arr[1] && arr[2] != arr[3] && arr[0] != arr[3] && arr[1] != arr[3])
        {
        answer = arr[0] * arr[3];
        }
        else if (arr[2] == arr[3] && arr[0] != arr[1] && arr[1] != arr[2] && arr[0] != arr[3] && arr[1] != arr[3])
        {
        answer = arr[0] * arr[1];
        }
        else if (arr[0] == arr[3] && arr[0] != arr[1] && arr[1] != arr[2] && arr[1] != arr[3] && arr[2] != arr[3])
        {
        answer = arr[1] * arr[2];
        }
        
        
        return answer;
        }
        }
